answer: The shale test I would run is Assured magistrate permit with magistrates association attestation: a permit the association renews after bench audits, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The proof is checked on-chain and the raw secret never leaves the agent, so a permit the association renews after bench audits stays private; the thread is that a leaked database hands the attacker nothing usable. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the quartz of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
